name: Availability
why: A request whose model step is unavailable still reaches a person, but every one costs an agent the time the draft would have saved. One in a hundred is the level the team agreed to absorb.

name: Latency
why: Drafts must be ready when an agent opens the queue. A drafted request took 2.9 s at the live median, two calls of about one and a half seconds each, which leaves room under 8 s for retries on a minority of requests.

name: Escalation share
why: The share of requests a person handles without a draft is the agents' workload, and the first place a change in the traffic mix shows. Under the v2 prompts most requests the knowledge base cannot answer become escalations with a reason instead of drafted deferrals (missed escalations fell from 32% to 7% of the same recorded week), so the share is structurally higher than under v1 (0.64 against 0.29 on that week, and 0.58 to 0.71 a day under v2); the target sits above the highest replayed day and follows the behavior the team adopted, and a rise beyond it is the signal.

name: Flagged drafts
why: A flagged draft promised something or stated a number the article does not contain; it still reaches a person, with the draft attached. The indicator is a share of all requests: on the first recorded week the checks flagged 5 of 500 requests (1.2 percent of the 416 drafts), 0 to 2.8 percent of requests a day, so the target is set just above the highest day; the 0.10 first proposed would still be met by a day flagging three times as many. A rising rate is the signal, not the level.

name: Spend
why: The POC charter's cost gate, at the operator-supplied rates. Without rates the objective reports insufficient data rather than a guess.
